run_findings.policy_evidence_lattice: Final merge readiness is a policy-family proof, not one CI boolean. Status checks have a strong exact-SHA connected verifier; required workflows are conditionally provable with generic Actions-run enumeration; reviews/signatures are only narrowly provable when all semantic dependencies are enumerable; required deployments, code scanning and code quality are UNKNOWN in the inspected connected surface because their public REST families are not connector-exposed; merge queue is a separate post-enqueue evidence stage.
run_findings.connector_public_probe: On public github/docs exact SHA 1beae09958f6eac6a4d82e5ee902d67f28dddda6, generic /actions/runs?head_sha=... returned exact-SHA workflow identity/status. Generic deployment, code-scanning-alert and code-quality-findings URLs were rejected at the connector allowlist and no dedicated read actions were discovered. Public PR review REST exposed commit_id that the normalized review wrapper omitted. Raw exact commit REST exposed commit.verification that the normalized commit wrapper omitted.
run_findings.review_boundary: GitHub review rules can depend on approval count, stale-review dismissal, code-owner review, latest-push approval, required teams/file patterns, conversation resolution, merge-base changes and even other open PRs sharing the same head commit. Therefore an APPROVED row count is not a general readiness proof. Explicit blocking evidence can prove BLOCKED; READY requires a narrow fully enumerable rule configuration.
run_findings.signature_boundary: Required signatures apply to every commit in the specified branch-update range, not just the head. Generic commit REST can expose verification, but complete range enumeration and final merge-method semantics are required before PASS.
run_findings.async_merge_protocol: Public merge-async is an exact-head crash/retry benchmark: submit sha=H plus explicit merge_action, persist 202 UUID, treat 409 existing UUID as ambiguous because options may differ, verify expected head/action via result readback, and remember result records expire after 24h. 202 is transaction acceptance, not merge completion; policy executes later in background. No connected async/queue mutation was discovered.
run_findings.atomic_vs_staged: GraphQL updateRefs gives atomic multi-ref CAS with per-ref beforeOid and all-or-nothing failure. Connected Contents operations are per-file blob-SHA CAS; safer multi-artifact publication is immutable payload(s) first then one CAS pointer as the commit point. File leases carry expiry/epoch metadata but cannot atomically acquire multiple files.
run_findings.new_rule_family: Current GitHub ruleset docs also expose code-coverage thresholds as a public-preview family. It belongs in the coverage lattice; no dedicated connected coverage/code-quality read action was discovered, so active coverage rules remain UNKNOWN without authoritative server evidence.
